name: Patañjali's eight limbs of yoga (aṣṭāṅga-yoga)

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Non-harming, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy and non-possessiveness; when unlimited by birth, place, time or circumstance they are the 'great vow' (YS 2.31).

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Purity, contentment, austerity, self-study and devotion to Īśvara.
stages.band_note: B1 as ethical-purificatory foundation; the last three observances are also the kriyā-yoga of YS 2.1 (B2 in kind).

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: Posture is steady and comfortable; mastered by relaxing effort and coalescing with the endless; from it, no assault by the pairs of opposites.

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: When posture is accomplished, the cutting off of the movement of in- and out-breath; from it the covering of the light dwindles and the mind becomes fit for concentration.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: The senses, disjoined from their objects, as it were imitate the mind's own form; from it, supreme mastery of the senses.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Binding the mind to a place.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: There, the continuous flow of a single cognition.
stages.band_note: B3 (upper edge): an unbroken flow on one object, not yet the object-only shining of samādhi.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: That same meditation when the object alone shines forth, as if empty of its own form. The last three limbs on one object are saṃyama (3.4); they are 'inner' relative to the first five (3.7) but 'outer' to seedless samādhi (3.8).
stages.band_note: B4: samādhi as a limb is absorption with an object (samprajñāta); the seedless state beyond it is B6 on pth:yoga-sutra-samadhi-ladder.

equivalents.note: Same eight limb-names re-described in the Yoga Yājñavalkya (ten yamas and ten niyamas; prāṇāyāma with nāḍī-purification).
Tirumūlar's eightfold (aṭṭāṅka) yoga in Tamil uses the same eight limbs inside a Śaiva frame.
The Purāṇic eight limbs follow the Pātañjala order.
Haribhadra himself pairs his eight views with the eight limbs (YDS 16), reinterpreting the limbs inwardly.
Five limb-names shared (without yama, niyama, āsana; with tarka); older six-limbed scheme.
The Gheraṇḍa replaces yama/niyama with the six cleansing acts and adds mudrā; four limb-names shared.

notes: YS 2.28: by practising the limbs impurity dwindles and the light of knowledge grows up to discriminative discernment (viveka-khyāti); the limbs therefore lead into pth:yoga-sutra-samadhi-ladder. The limbs are not all strictly sequential in the bhāṣya (yama and niyama are kept throughout); the order of the list is the sūtra's.

name: The ladder of samādhi in the Yoga Sūtra (samāpatti → viveka-khyāti → nirbīja → dharmamegha → kaivalya)

stages.name: savitarkā samāpatti
stages.description: Coalescence on a gross object mixed with the conceptual constructions of word, object and knowledge.

stages.name: nirvitarkā samāpatti
stages.description: When memory is purified, the object alone shines forth as if empty of its own form.

stages.name: savicārā samāpatti
stages.description: The same, on subtle objects (delimited by place, time and cause, per the bhāṣya).

stages.name: nirvicārā samāpatti
stages.description: On subtle objects without such delimitation; subtlety ends in the unmarked (aliṅga, 1.45). These four are 'with seed' (sabīja, 1.46).

stages.name: sānanda
stages.description: The third form of samprajñāta samādhi named in YS 1.17: joy; the bhāṣya explains it as a samādhi accompanied by bliss after reasoning and reflection have dropped.
stages.band_note: The sūtra lists vitarka, vicāra, ānanda, asmitā (1.17) and separately the four samāpattis (1.42-44); ordering them into one ladder is the commentators' (bhāṣya and sub-commentaries).

stages.name: sāsmitā
stages.description: The fourth form of samprajñāta: awareness of a single self (ekātmikā saṃvit) per the bhāṣya.

stages.name: adhyātma-prasāda, ṛtambharā prajñā, viveka-khyāti
stages.gloss: inner clarity, truth-bearing insight, discriminative discernment
stages.description: In the lucidity of nirvicāra there is inner clarity (1.47); there insight is truth-bearing (1.48), having the particular as object (1.49); unwavering discriminative discernment of sattva and puruṣa is the means of avoidance (2.26) and grounds the sevenfold final insight (2.27).

stages.name: asamprajñāta / nirbīja samādhi
stages.description: Preceded by practice of the cognition of cessation, with only residual impressions (1.18); when even the impression born of truth-bearing insight is stilled, everything is stilled — seedless samādhi (1.50-51). Its means is higher dispassion (1.16; YBh 1.18).
stages.band_note: Asamprajñāta (1.18) and nirbīja (1.51) are identified by the commentators; banded B6 as the deepening after discernment.

stages.name: dharmamegha samādhi
stages.description: For one who takes no interest even in the highest reflection, from complete discriminative discernment comes the samādhi called cloud of dharma (4.29); from it afflictions and karma cease (4.30), and the bhāṣya says the knower is then liberated while living.
stages.band_note: The band scheme mentions 'dharmamegha as culmination' under B8; in the Yoga Sūtra dharmamegha is the last samādhi before kaivalya and is not activity in the world, so it is banded B6 (as on pth:yoga-sutra-kaivalya-sequence); its fruit, cessation of afflictions and karma (4.30), is B7.

stages.name: kaivalya
stages.description: When sattva and puruṣa are equal in purity (3.55); the return of the guṇas, empty of purpose for the puruṣa, to their source — or the power of consciousness established in its own form (4.34).

equivalents.note: Bhoja's version of the same ladder (RM 1.17-18) with viveka-khyāti as a seventh samprajñāta rung.
Continuation of the top of this ladder in YS 4.25-34 (same dharmamegha → kaivalya segment).
Both are graded absorptions refining away coarser factors (vitarka/vicāra in both vocabularies); the Yoga Sūtra's goal (puruṣa's isolation) and the Buddhist cessation are not claimed to be the same.

notes: Correction to the unit brief: the sūtra itself gives two lists (1.17: vitarka, vicāra, ānanda, asmitā; 1.42-44: four samāpattis) — the single ladder savitarka→…→asmitā is the commentators' synthesis; 'sa-/nir-' pairs for ānanda and asmitā are later (sub-commentaries). The sūtra does not itself equate asamprajñāta (1.18) with nirbīja (1.51); the commentators do.

name: The seven means of the 'yoga of the pot' (ghaṭastha-yoga) in the Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā

stages.name: śodhana through ṣaṭkarma
stages.description: Dhauti, vasti, neti, laulikī, trāṭaka and kapālabhāti cleanse the body (the unbaked pot to be fired in the fire of yoga).
stages.band_note: B1 by the text's own word śodhana (purification) — bodily, not ethical, purification; some acts of this chapter are restricted (summary only).

stages.name: dṛḍhatā through āsana
stages.description: Of the eighty-four lakh postures taught by Śiva, thirty-two are described.

stages.name: sthiratā through mudrā
stages.description: Twenty-five mudrās (mahāmudrā, bandhas, khecarī, viparītakaraṇī, śakticālana and others).
stages.band_note: Several of these seals are restricted practices (khecarī, vajroṇī): summary only.

stages.name: dhairya through pratyāhāra
stages.description: Wherever the fickle mind wanders, it is drawn back and brought under the control of the self.

stages.name: lāghava through prāṇāyāma
stages.description: After place, time, moderate diet and purification of the channels, eight kinds of retention (kumbhaka) are taught.
stages.band_note: Banded B2 by kind (breath discipline) although the text places it after withdrawal; the order is the Gheraṇḍa's own and is kept.

stages.name: pratyakṣa through dhyāna
stages.gloss: direct perception (of the self) through meditation
stages.description: Meditation is threefold — gross (on a form), of light, and subtle (on bindu/kuṇḍalinī) — and yields 'direct perception in the self'.
stages.band_note: Banded by the fruit the text names (pratyakṣam ātmani, direct perception of the self, B5); the practice itself — visualized form, light, bindu — is absorption with support (B4).

stages.name: nirliptatva through samādhi
stages.description: Samādhi, obtained by the guru's grace, is separating the mind from the body and uniting it with the supreme self: 'I am Brahman'; 'through samādhi, untaintedness, and liberation without doubt'.

equivalents.note: Stage 7 is expanded into six kinds of samādhi in GhS 7.
Four limb-names shared (āsana, pratyāhāra, prāṇāyāma, dhyāna, samādhi); yama/niyama replaced by bodily cleansing; mudrā added; order of prāṇāyāma and pratyāhāra reversed.

notes: Verified locally against the DCS text of the Gheraṇḍasaṃhitā (1.10-11: śodhanaṃ dṛḍhatā caiva sthairyaṃ dhairyaṃ ca lāghavam / pratyakṣaṃ ca nirliptaṃ ca …; ṣaṭkarmaṇā śodhanaṃ … samādhinā nirliptaṃ ca muktir eva na saṃśayaḥ). The chapter order of the text follows the seven means.

name: The six-limbed yoga of the Maitrī Upaniṣad (ṣaḍaṅga-yoga)

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: First limb of the method (prayoga-kalpa) for union with the self.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: The mind withdrawn from outer things and the objects placed within (6.19).

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Named before dhāraṇā in this list.
stages.band_note: The Maitrī's order puts dhyāna before dhāraṇā; both banded B3.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: The 'further concentration' of 6.20: pressing the tongue-tip to the palate, restraining speech, mind and breath.

stages.name: tarka
stages.description: A limb peculiar to this list; in 6.20 'by tarka one sees brahman'.
stages.band_note: B4 as discernment still working with an object; the seeing it leads to is stage 7.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Last limb; the mind placed in what is not mind, the inconceivable, without support (6.19).

stages.name: seeing the golden-hued maker
stages.description: By this yoga the seer sees the golden-coloured maker, the lord, the person, the source of brahman (brahmayoni); through the dissolution of mind one sees the self, subtler than the subtle, shining (6.20).

stages.name: making all one in the imperishable
stages.description: The knower, leaving merit and evil, makes all one in the highest imperishable; faults do not approach him, as deer and birds avoid a burning mountain; selflessness is 'the mark of liberation' (6.20).

equivalents.note: Same count of six and three shared limb-names (pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, samādhi) in a different order, with anusmṛti for tarka; no historical claim is made here.
As above: six limbs with five shared names; Kālacakra has anusmṛti where the Maitrī has tarka.
Nātha six-limbed yoga (āsana instead of tarka).
Six-limbed yoga of the Yoga Upaniṣads.
The Amṛtanāda Upaniṣad's six limbs (pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, tarka, samādhi) keep tarka as in the Maitrī.

notes: Stage names and order verified against the local e-text (Cowell recension, ebharati): prāṇāyāmaḥ pratyāhāro dhyānaṃ dhāraṇā tarkaḥ samādhiḥ ṣaḍaṅga ity ucyate yogaḥ (6.18). Stages 7-8 are the fruit stated in the same section; they are added so that the map reaches its own goal.

name: The four yogas of the Dattātreyayogaśāstra (mantra, laya, haṭha, rāja)

stages.name: mantrayoga
stages.description: Placing the mātṛkā letters on the limbs and repeating a mantra; for the mild (mṛdu) practitioner, called the lowest of yogas; in twelve years knowledge and powers.

stages.name: layayoga
stages.description: Dissolution of mind through 'indications' (saṅketa), of which Ādinātha taught eight crore — e.g. meditating on the void, gazing at the nose-tip or between the brows, lying like a corpse.

stages.name: haṭhayoga
stages.description: Twofold: the eight limbs known to Yājñavalkya, and the mudrās of Kapila (mahāmudrā, mahābandha, mahāvedha, khecarī, the bandhas, viparītakaraṇī, vajrolī …); its course runs through the four stages ārambha → niṣpatti.
stages.band_note: B2 as the discipline itself; its course spans B2-B7 on pth:hatha-four-stages. Vajrolī and related practices are restricted (summary only).

stages.name: rājayoga
stages.description: 'The fourth, the best of yogas'; it arises in due time from practising all the above; attaining it the yogin may act or not act as he pleases — the stage of consummation giving enjoyment and liberation.
stages.band_note: B7: the text's goal-state (samādhi, liberation while living, DYŚ 111-114); the yogin's free activity after it would be B8.

equivalents.note: The Yogatattva Upaniṣad repeats the same four yogas (it draws on the Dattātreyayogaśāstra).
Gorakṣa's Amaraughaprabodha names the same four yogas and grades them by practitioner.

notes: The four are graded by the practitioner's capacity (adhikāra) — the Śiva Saṃhitā (5.10-14) assigns mantra to the mild, laya to the middling, haṭha to the strong and all to the strongest aspirant — so they are not a strict sequence; but DYŚ 145-147 says rājayoga arises from haṭha practice and ŚS 5.181 that haṭha and rāja need each other. Hence the non-monotonic bands (B2, B3, B2, B7).

name: The four stages of yoga practice (ārambha, ghaṭa, paricaya, niṣpatti)

stages.name: ārambha
stages.description: With the channels purified, signs appear (lightness, radiance, sweat, trembling, hopping); in the Haṭhayogapradīpikā the knot of Brahmā is pierced and the tinkling unstruck sound is heard with bliss from the void.
stages.band_note: B2 in the DYŚ/ŚS account (signs of breath-discipline); the HYP's nāda version already begins at B3 (so U28's pth:hyp-nada-four-stages).

stages.name: ghaṭa
stages.description: Prāṇa and apāna, nāda and bindu, the individual and the supreme self 'meet'; sense-withdrawal while established in retention; in the HYP the breath, made one, enters the middle and the knot of Viṣṇu is pierced (kettledrum sound).

stages.name: paricaya
stages.description: The breath enters suṣumnā unobstructed with the awakened kuṇḍalinī; the fivefold element-concentrations; in the HYP the breath reaches the great void, sound of a drum, natural bliss.

stages.name: niṣpatti
stages.description: Rājayoga: the seeds of karma are crossed and samādhi arises for the one liberated while living (ŚS); the knot of Rudra is pierced, flute and vīṇā sounds, the mind becomes one (HYP); the stage gives both enjoyment and liberation (DYŚ).

equivalents.note: The Haṭhayogapradīpikā's account of the same four stages through inner sound and the three knots.
The Śiva Saṃhitā's account of the same four stages.
The Yogatattva Upaniṣad's account of the same four stages.
Both describe the breath/kuṇḍalinī passing the knots or centres up the central channel.

notes: Umbrella map for the four avasthās 'in all yogas' (HYP 4.69; ŚS 3.31; DYŚ 9-10), first taught in the Amṛtasiddhi. The texts describe the stages chiefly through breath-retention and its signs; retention counts and durations are deliberately omitted (restricted). The existing text-specific maps (U28, U29, U04) are the detailed versions; this map aligns them.

name: The seven stages of knowledge (jñāna-bhūmikā) of the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha

stages.name: śubhecchā
stages.description: Preceded by dispassion, the wish: 'why do I remain a fool? I shall look to scripture and the good.'

stages.name: vicāraṇā
stages.description: The turn to right conduct through contact with scripture and the good, with dispassion and practice.
stages.band_note: B2 as scripture-based inquiry and practice; it includes the turn to right conduct (B1 in kind).

stages.name: tanumānasā
stages.description: From the first two, non-attachment to sense-objects; desire is thinned.

stages.name: sattvāpatti
stages.description: From practice of these three, the mind rests in pure sattva, the self; Vidyāraṇya calls one here a 'knower of Brahman' (brahmavid).

stages.name: asaṃsakti
stages.description: Detachment from all things through the maturing of the fourth; the knower rises from absorption by himself (brahmavid-vara).

stages.name: padārthābhāvanī
stages.description: Things outside and inside cease to present themselves; he rises from absorption only when roused by others (varīyān).

stages.name: turyagā
stages.description: Abiding in the self alone; this belongs to those liberated while living, who, when prompted, follow customary conduct 'like one half-asleep' (variṣṭha).
stages.band_note: B7 as the attainment of liberation while living; the liberated one's unaffected customary conduct is a B8 facet of the same stage.

stages.name: turyātīta
stages.description: The domain of the bodiless liberated (videhamukta), beyond the seven stages; 'liberation lies beyond the seven'.

equivalents.note: The Varāha Upaniṣad gives the same seven stages (tanumānasī, padārthabhāvanā as variant spellings).
The Mahā Upaniṣad pairs these seven stages of knowledge with seven stages of ignorance.
Vidyāraṇya's Pañcadaśī 7 gives a different sevenfold series of the jīva's states (ignorance → satisfaction).
Graded knowers in the Yoga tradition (the bhāṣya's four kinds of yogin).

notes: Vasiṣṭha himself says the first three stages are 'waking-like' states of the seeker, the fourth dream-like, the fifth deep-sleep-like, the sixth and seventh turya and beyond (Mokṣopāya 6.140-156); Vidyāraṇya's Jīvanmuktiviveka grades the knower as brahmavid (4), brahmavid-vara (5), varīyān (6), variṣṭha (7). Stage 8 (turyātīta) is stated in the same passage and added to reach the text's own end.

name: The Advaita course of practice: purification → fourfold means → hearing, reflection, contemplation → liberation while living → bodiless liberation

stages.name: citta-śuddhi through karma and upāsanā
stages.gloss: purifying the mind by rites and meditations
stages.description: Obligatory daily and occasional rites, expiations and meditations, with desire-prompted and forbidden acts avoided, purify the mind; action purifies but does not reach the Real.

stages.name: sādhana-catuṣṭaya
stages.description: Discrimination of the eternal and non-eternal; dispassion toward enjoyments here and hereafter; the six treasures (calm, self-control, withdrawal, forbearance, faith, concentration); longing for liberation — after which the inquiry into Brahman begins ('atha').
stages.band_note: B0 because the tradition presents these as the qualification (adhikāra) for inquiry; the six treasures are disciplines (B1-B3 in kind).

stages.name: guru-upasatti
stages.description: To know the unmade, the disenchanted seeker goes, fuel in hand, to a teacher learned in scripture and established in Brahman.

stages.name: śravaṇa
stages.description: Determining, by the six marks of purport, that the Upaniṣads teach the non-dual Brahman; for the best qualified a single hearing of 'that you are' suffices.
stages.band_note: B2 as study of scripture; for the uttama-adhikārin hearing itself yields knowledge (B5).

stages.name: manana
stages.description: Continual consideration of what was heard by reasoning in accord with it, removing doubt.

stages.name: nididhyāsana
stages.description: The flow of like cognitions excluding unlike ones; its auxiliaries are the savikalpa and nirvikalpa samādhis of the Vedāntasāra.

stages.name: aparokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: The knowledge arising from the great sentence (mahāvākya) that removes ignorance; the knower's past sins are destroyed and future ones do not touch him.

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: The body continues until the karma that has begun to bear fruit (prārabdha) is exhausted, like a potter's wheel still turning; 'he waits only so long'; he attains Brahman here.

stages.name: the liberated one's life for the world
stages.description: The peaceful great ones who have crossed the ocean live like the spring, doing good to the world and helping others across; the purposes of jīvanmukti include protecting knowledge and manifesting bliss.

stages.name: videhamukti
stages.description: At the fall of the body the prāṇas of the knower of the attributeless Brahman do not depart; being Brahman he merges in Brahman. (Worshippers of the qualified Brahman go by the path of light and are liberated gradually.)

equivalents.note: Expands stage 6 (the auxiliaries of nididhyāsana: savikalpa and nirvikalpa samādhi).
Śaṅkara-attributed fifteen limbs of 'rāja-yoga' re-described as knowledge; a parallel Advaita path.
Vidyāraṇya's Jīvanmuktiviveka uses the seven bhūmikās to grade Advaita knowers (stages 4-7 ~ this map's 7-9).
Dvaita also teaches śravaṇa-manana-nididhyāsana leading to aparokṣa-jñāna, but of the Lord as other than the self; Dvaita rejects the identity this map's stage 7 names.

tradition_objection: Advaita holds that liberation is not produced by any stage: Brahman is ever-attained and knowledge only removes ignorance. The stages are for removing obstacles according to the student's fitness (adhikāra); for the best student a single hearing of the great sentence is enough (BSBh 4.1.2). The Vivaraṇa school makes hearing the principal means and reflection and contemplation its auxiliaries; the Bhāmatī school gives contemplation (prasaṅkhyāna) a larger role.
notes: Uses existing U03/U13 teachings. Stage 9 (the liberated one's life) is placed before videhamukti because it belongs to the living knower.

name: The four pādas of Śaiva Siddhānta (caryā, kriyā, yoga, jñāna) and their fruits

stages.name: iruvinaiyoppu, malaparipāka, śaktinipāta
stages.gloss: balance of the two deeds, ripening of mala, descent of grace
stages.description: When good and bad karma balance and the soul's mala ripens, Śiva's power descends in four grades (very mild … very intense), fitting the soul for caryā, kriyā, yoga or jñāna; Śiva comes as the guru.

stages.name: caryā (dāsa-mārga)
stages.description: Outer service of the Lord (in the Tamil tradition: temple service); its fruit is sālokya, dwelling in Śiva's world.
stages.band_note: B2 as devotional-ritual practice; the Siddhānta counts it as a real path with its own (lower) liberation.

stages.name: kriyā (satputra-mārga)
stages.gloss: ritual worship — the good son's path
stages.description: Worship (pūjā) of Śiva, outer and inner; fruit sāmīpya, nearness.

stages.name: yoga (saha-mārga)
stages.description: Inner yoga of the eight limbs directed to Śiva; fruit sārūpya, likeness of form.

stages.name: jñāna (san-mārga)
stages.description: Given by the guru's grace; proceeds by hearing, reflection, clarity and abiding (kēṭṭal, cintittal, teḷital, niṭṭai); the soul sees Śiva in itself with the eye of grace and knows the senses' world as a mirage.
stages.band_note: Begins at B5 (recognition through the guru); its 'abiding' (niṭṭai) is B6.

stages.name: sāyujya / aṇaintu nirral
stages.description: The soul, one with the Lord as his servant, is no longer touched by mala, māyā and the two deeds; by unforgetting love it reaches his feet — inseparable, not identical.

stages.name: worship of the devotees and the temple
stages.description: Having washed away the three malas, the freed soul joins the true devotees and worships their holy garb and the temple as the Lord.

equivalents.note: The Tamil ten acts (tacakāriyam) articulate the jñāna-pāda's culmination.
Both lead through devotional practice to a relational culmination (union as servant; prema) rather than identity.
Both end in liberation through knowledge given by grace/teaching; the Siddhānta rejects Advaita's identity of soul and Śiva (sāyujya is inseparability, not identity).

tradition_objection: The Siddhānta insists that in liberation the soul neither becomes Śiva nor perishes but abides inseparable from him (Cittiyār cupakkam 11); an equivalence of stage 6 with Advaita's jīvanmukti/videhamukti holds only as 'same band', not same state.
notes: In the Āgamas the four pādas are also the four sections of an Āgama (vidyā/jñāna, kriyā, yoga, caryā). Tirumūlar teaches that each pāda contains the others in miniature (caryā-in-caryā … jñāna-in-jñāna), so the four are not strictly exclusive stages. The first three yield the lower liberations (sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya) and ripen the soul; only jñāna gives sāyujya.

name: The four means (upāya) of the Trika: āṇava, śākta, śāmbhava, anupāya

stages.name: āṇavopāya (kriyopāya)
stages.description: Immersion (samāveśa) through meditation on the breath (uccāra), bodily seals (karaṇa), visualization (dhyāna), letters (varṇa) and the positing of places (sthāna-kalpanā); its signs are bliss, leaping, trembling, sleep and whirling.
stages.ref: MVT 2.21; TĀ ch.5; Śiva Sūtra section 3
stages.band_note: B2 in kind (supported practices of breath, body, visualization and place), reaching B3-B4 in its own immersion.

stages.name: śāktopāya (jñānopāya)
stages.description: Immersion by contemplating with the mind alone a reality free of utterance; purification of thought-constructs (vikalpa-saṃskāra) by pure reasoning (sattarka), the teacher's instruction and scripture; the wheel of consciousness and the Kālīs.
stages.ref: MVT 2.22; TĀ ch.4; Śiva Sūtra section 2

stages.name: śāmbhavopāya (icchopāya)
stages.description: Immersion that arises for one who thinks of nothing, through the awakening given by the teacher; the universe appears in consciousness like a reflection in a mirror.
stages.ref: MVT 2.23; TĀ ch.3; Śiva Sūtra section 1

stages.name: anupāya (later also ānandopāya)
stages.description: For one of the highest grace a single hearing of the teacher's word suffices; nothing is to be done, since what is attained is one's own ever-present nature; once Śivahood is known with conviction, nothing further is to be done by any instrument.
stages.band_note: B7 by what it names (no further means; Śivahood known); the tradition does not treat it as a stage one climbs to.

equivalents.note: Both hold that recognition of one's own nature can be immediate for some while others proceed by graded means; not claimed to be the same recognition.
Dzogchen and the Trika both speak of a means-less recognition; each tradition's account of what is recognized differs and neither endorses the equation.

tradition_objection: The four are means (upāya) matched to the intensity of the descent of grace (TĀ 13), not rungs everyone must climb: the one of highest grace needs no means, and one may enter directly at śāmbhava. Abhinavagupta does teach that the lower means culminate in the higher and that difference of means does not make liberation different (TĀ 1.165-166); the Tantrāloka expounds them from the highest downward (chs. 2-5).
notes: Correction to the brief: 'anupāya' is Abhinavagupta's term (TĀ 2); the name ānandopāya for it is later. Kṣemarāja reads the three sections of the Śiva Sūtra as śāmbhava, śākta and āṇava means. The stages are listed here in ascending order for the correspondence table; the tradition's own order of exposition is descending.

name: The six stages (ṣaṭsthala) of the Vīraśaiva path

stages.name: bhakta
stages.description: One in whom devotion to Śiva has arisen; the dharmas he practises are the bhakta-sthala (initiation, wearing the liṅga, worship of guru, liṅga and jaṅgama); its bhakti is faith; its liṅga the ācāra-liṅga.
stages.band_note: B0 by its bhakti (faith) and entry through liṅga-dīkṣā; its daily worship is B2 in kind.

stages.name: māheśvara
stages.description: Devotion risen to excellence through dispassion; turned away from the stations of Brahmā and the other gods; steadfast in vows and in the liṅga; guru-liṅga.

stages.name: prasādī
stages.gloss: the recipient of grace — with attentiveness (avadhāna)
stages.description: His bonds destroyed through steadfastness, he attains serenity of mind (manaḥ-prasāda); offering everything to the liṅga, he receives it as grace; śiva-liṅga.

stages.name: prāṇaliṅgī
stages.gloss: one whose liṅga is the breath — with experience (anubhava)
stages.description: Beginning of the knowledge-predominant sthalas: the liṅga is known as brahman of the nature of consciousness, its power the breath; worship of the inner liṅga of consciousness; cara/jaṅgama-liṅga.
stages.band_note: B5: first of the three knowledge-predominant sthalas; recognition of the liṅga as consciousness (its inner worship has B4 aspects).

stages.name: śaraṇa
stages.description: The aṅga-liṅgī whose form is knowledge is the wife (satī) and Śiva the husband (pati); the bliss of their union; prasāda-liṅga.

stages.name: aikya
stages.description: Through contemplation of oneness with Śiva, immersion in the great ocean of Śiva's bliss; the self dissolved in the sky of consciousness by equal flavour; mahā-liṅga.

equivalents.note: The 101 sub-sthalas of the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi subdivide these six.
Both ascend by kinds of devotion (faith → steadiness → … → union / prema).

notes: Each sthala is paired with one of six liṅgas (ācāra, guru, śiva, cara/jaṅgama, prasāda, mahā) and six forms of devotion (śraddhā, niṣṭhā, avadhāna, anubhava, ānanda, samarasa; cf. cpt:sadvidha-bhakti). The first three are 'action-predominant', the last three 'knowledge-predominant' (SŚ 12.2-3). The vacanakāras (Basava, Allama, Cennabasava) use the same six stages in Kannada.

name: Rūpa Gosvāmī's sequence of the arising of love (premṇaḥ prādurbhāve kramaḥ)

stages.name: śraddhā
stages.description: First, faith.

stages.name: sādhu-saṅga
stages.description: Then the company of holy devotees.

stages.name: bhajana-kriyā
stages.description: Then the practice of devotion (the limbs of sādhana-bhakti: hearing, chanting, remembering, service …).

stages.name: anartha-nivṛtti
stages.description: Then what is unwanted falls away.
stages.band_note: B1 by kind (purification), kept in the text's order after practice.

stages.name: niṣṭhā
stages.description: Then steadiness.

stages.name: ruci
stages.description: Then taste (relish) for devotion.

stages.name: āsakti
stages.description: Then attachment.

stages.name: bhāva (rati)
stages.description: Then bhāva: of the nature of special pure sattva, like a ray of the sun of prema, softening the heart; its signs are forbearance, not wasting time, detachment, freedom from pride, hope, longing, taste for the name …

stages.name: prema
stages.description: Then love rises: bhāva become dense, thoroughly softening the heart, marked by an excess of possessiveness toward the Lord.
stages.band_note: B7 as the tradition's final goal (prayojana); the Gauḍīyas deny that prema is the same as mokṣa — they hold it makes liberation trivial (BRS 1.1.17).

equivalents.note: Viśvanātha Cakravartin's Mādhurya-kādambinī expounds the same nine stages (subdividing practice and the anarthas); bands identical.
Continues stage 9: prema → sneha → māna → praṇaya → rāga → anurāga → mahābhāva.
Nārada's aphorisms also lead from renunciation and company of the great to love.

tradition_objection: Prema is the 'fifth goal of life' beyond liberation; Rūpa's tradition rejects any reading of it as merging (sāyujya) and treats desire for liberation as an obstacle ('the witch of desire for enjoyment and liberation', BRS 1.2.22).
notes: Verse verified locally (GRETIL Haribhaktirasāmṛtasindhu 1.4.15-16: ādau śraddhā tataḥ sādhusaṅgo 'tha bhajanakriyā / tato 'narthanivṛttiḥ syāt tato niṣṭhā rucis tataḥ // athāsaktis tato bhāvas tataḥ premābhyudañcati / sādhakānām ayaṃ premṇaḥ prādurbhāve bhavet kramaḥ). Rūpa says this is 'the sequence for practitioners' (sādhakānām); those graced otherwise may skip it.

name: The fourteen stages of quality (guṇasthāna)

stages.name: mithyādṛṣṭi
stages.description: The soul under the rise of view-deluding karma; the approach to right view (the three processes, apunarbandhaka state) happens at its end.
stages.band_note: Starting condition, unbanded; the approach at its end (yathāpravṛtta-, apūrva-, anivṛtti-karaṇa) is B0 on other maps.

stages.name: sāsādana (sāsvādana)
stages.description: A momentary stage passed only while falling from subsidential right view toward wrong view, with a lingering taste of right view.
stages.band_note: A stage of descent only; unbanded.

stages.name: samyag-mithyādṛṣṭi (miśra)
stages.description: A mixed state of right and wrong view, like curd mixed with sugar.
stages.band_note: B0: wavering at the threshold of right view.

stages.name: avirata-samyagdṛṣṭi
stages.description: Right view (samyaktva) attained — conviction in the realities as they are, with the 'knot' broken — but without vows.
stages.band_note: B5 by the tradition's own claim that right view is the root and first real seeing of the path (the knot broken; in the Digambara adhyātma account, experience of the self); TS 1.2 defines it as conviction (śraddhāna), which on other maps would sit at B0 — contested.

stages.name: deśavirata (saṃyatāsaṃyata)
stages.description: The layman's partial vows (aṇuvrata).
stages.band_note: B1 by kind (vows), after B5 — Jainism puts right view before conduct.

stages.name: pramatta-saṃyata
stages.description: Full vows of the mendicant, with carelessness (pramāda) still arising.

stages.name: apramatta-saṃyata
stages.description: Restraint without carelessness; virtuous meditation (dharma-dhyāna) prevails.

stages.name: apūrvakaraṇa
stages.description: Beginning of the ascent on one of the two ladders (subsidence or destruction); pure meditation (śukla-dhyāna) begins.
stages.band_note: B4: first pure meditation 'with multiplicity and reasoning' still works with scriptural thought (TS 9.41-43).

stages.name: anivṛtti-bādara-sāmparāya
stages.gloss: the non-returning process with gross passion
stages.description: Gross passions are subsided or destroyed.

stages.name: sūkṣma-sāmparāya
stages.description: Only subtle greed remains.

stages.name: upaśānta-moha
stages.description: Delusion wholly subsided but not destroyed; the soul falls back from here.
stages.band_note: B6, but a dead end: from subsidence the soul necessarily falls back.

stages.name: kṣīṇa-moha
stages.description: All deluding karma destroyed; the second pure meditation (unity, without shifting); then the other destructive karmas are destroyed.

stages.name: sayoga-kevalin
stages.description: Omniscience (kevala-jñāna); the Jina lives and teaches while body, speech and mind still act.
stages.band_note: B7: kevala-jñāna is the tradition's liberation-knowledge; the teaching activity of the embodied Jina is a B8 facet.

stages.name: ayoga-kevalin
stages.description: All activity stopped for the time of uttering five short syllables; the last pure meditation; then liberation (the siddha, beyond the guṇasthānas).

equivalents.note: Umāsvāti's ten grades of karma-shedding (TS 9.45) run parallel to guṇasthānas 4-13.
Haribhadra's first four views fall within guṇasthāna 1; sthirā onward correspond to right view (4) and above; parā to kevala.
External self ~ guṇasthānas 1-3; internal self ~ 4-12; supreme self ~ 13-14 (Pūjyapāda's Samādhitantra).
The four pure meditations are distributed over guṇasthānas 8-14.

Right view (4) and stream-entry are both the first irreversible seeing that bounds the remaining rebirths; the Jain soul-doctrine and the Buddhist not-self teaching are not reconciled by this correspondence.

notes: Stage names follow the Gommaṭasāra Jīvakāṇḍa 9-10 (and the Ṣaṭkhaṇḍāgama); the Śvetāmbara lists agree in substance. The guṇasthānas are classes of soul-state by the operation of mohanīya karma and activity, not only a practice ladder: a soul may fall from 11 (and from 4 via 2). Beyond 14 the liberated soul (siddha) is outside the guṇasthānas.

name: Haribhadra's eight views of yoga (yoga-dṛṣṭi)

stages.name: mitrā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: friendly — like straw-fire spark; limb: yama; fault removed: fatigue (kheda); quality: non-aversion (adveṣa)
stages.description: The dim first view: restraints present as wish, no weariness in worship, no aversion; the 'seeds of yoga' (devotion to the Jina, service of teachers, disgust with existence) are sown.
stages.band_note: B0 as the sowing of the seeds of yoga; Haribhadra pairs it with yama (B1).

stages.name: tārā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: star-like — like cow-dung fire; limb: niyama; fault removed: anxiety (udvega); quality: desire to know (jijñāsā)
stages.description: Observances appear; no anxiety in doing good; desire to know the truth.

stages.name: balā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: strong — like wood fire; limb: āsana; fault removed: distraction (kṣepa); quality: desire to hear (śuśrūṣā)
stages.description: Posture steady, restlessness gone, longing to hear the truth.

stages.name: dīprā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: shining — like lamp; limb: prāṇāyāma; fault removed: interruption (utthāna); quality: hearing (śravaṇa)
stages.description: Breath-control in an inner sense (expelling outer states, taking in inner ones); the truth is heard, but the subtle knot is not yet broken.

stages.name: sthirā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: steady — like gem; limb: pratyāhāra; fault removed: error (bhrānti); quality: understanding (bodha)
stages.description: The knot is broken and right view arises; worldly doings look like children's houses of dust.
stages.band_note: B5 by the Jain criterion (right view, knot broken); Haribhadra's paired limb, pratyāhāra, would be B3 on the Pātañjala map — both recorded.

stages.name: kāntā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: lovely — like star; limb: dhāraṇā; fault removed: delight in other things (anyamud); quality: reflection (mīmāṃsā)
stages.description: Concentration firm; acting in the world with the mind fixed on dharma.

stages.name: prabhā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: radiant — like sun; limb: dhyāna; fault removed: affliction/disease (ruj); quality: practice (pratipatti)
stages.description: Meditation prevails with its happiness; activity free of attachment — what others call the peaceful flow and the way of Śiva.

stages.name: parā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: supreme — like moon; limb: samādhi; fault removed: attachment (āsaṅga); quality: right engagement (pravṛtti)
stages.description: Absorption free of attachment; beyond practices; omniscience; renouncing even yoga (yoga-saṃnyāsa), liberation.

sources.ref: 13-16 and the sections on each view

equivalents.note: Haribhadra pairs the views with Patañjali's limbs (YDS 16), reinterpreted inwardly; stated by the text itself.
The first four views lie within guṇasthāna 1 (ogha-dṛṣṭi); sthirā begins right view (4+); parā is kevala (13-14).
Haribhadra's four kinds of yogin grade the same practitioners by family and progress.

notes: The eight faults and eight qualities are given from memory of YDS 16 and its auto-commentary (moderate confidence on the exact pairing). Haribhadra addresses yogins of other schools too (YDS 129-134: the omniscient teachers of different schools are not really different), so the views are meant to be applicable across traditions. The first four views are unstable (they can fall back); the last four are stable.

name: Hemacandra's four kinds of mind and the no-mind state (Yogaśāstra 12)

stages.name: vikṣipta
stages.description: Restless.
stages.band_note: Starting condition, unbanded.

stages.name: yātāyāta
stages.description: Goes out and returns; has some bliss.

stages.name: śliṣṭa
stages.description: Steady and blissful.

stages.name: sulīna
stages.description: Very steady, with the highest bliss.

stages.name: unmanībhāva
stages.description: When the mind is left alone in indifference it becomes still of itself; in the no-mind state the self is realised and the yogin, like one freed of a load, experiences bliss.
stages.band_note: B5 by the text's claim that the self is realised here; low confidence on verse numbers.

equivalents.note: Graded minds/practitioners in the Yoga tradition; Vyāsa's five levels of mind (kṣipta … niruddha, YBh 1.1) are a closer analogue.

notes: Hemacandra introduces chapter 12 as the reality established by his own experience (12.1), after eleven chapters drawn from scripture. The four minds are also named in the Amanaska tradition of 'no-mind'; no borrowing claim is made here.

name: The three trainings (tisso sikkhā / triśikṣā): virtue, concentration, wisdom

stages.name: adhisīla-sikkhā
stages.description: Restraint by the Pātimokkha, the monk's virtue (abstaining from killing, stealing, unchastity, false speech …) that brings blameless happiness; right speech, action and livelihood belong here.

stages.name: adhicitta-sikkhā
stages.description: The four jhānas; right effort, mindfulness and concentration belong here; unification of mind is concentration, the four establishments of mindfulness its signs.
stages.band_note: B4 as the jhānas; its preparatory mindfulness and effort are B3.

stages.name: adhipaññā-sikkhā
stages.description: Knowing the four noble truths as they really are; right view and intention belong here.
stages.band_note: B5 as knowing the truths as they are (the path's seeing); its maturing through the higher paths is B6.

stages.name: vimutti
stages.description: The mind imbued with wisdom is rightly freed from the effluents of sensuality, becoming and ignorance.

equivalents.note: The Visuddhimagga expounds its seven purifications within the frame of virtue, concentration and understanding.
The gradual training of DN 2 / MN 27 unfolds the three trainings step by step.
Ethical restraints → concentration → discernment in both; the Yoga Sūtra's goal (isolation of puruṣa) is not the Buddhist liberation.

notes: Pan-Buddhist frame (Pali, Sarvāstivāda, Mahāyāna and Tibetan lamrim all use it). Stage 4 (vimutti) is the fruit named in the recurrent DN 16 talk; the local Pali root text was checked for that quotation.

name: The nine successive abidings (anupubbavihāra): four jhānas, four formless attainments, cessation

stages.name: upacāra-samādhi (commentarial)
stages.description: Unification reached just before absorption, when the hindrances are suppressed and the counterpart sign arises; not part of the canonical nine.

stages.name: paṭhama jhāna
stages.description: Secluded from sense pleasures and unwholesome states, with applied and sustained thought, rapture and bliss born of seclusion; sensual perception ceases in it.

stages.name: dutiya jhāna
stages.description: With applied and sustained thought stilled: inner confidence, unification, rapture and bliss born of concentration.

stages.name: tatiya jhāna
stages.description: With the fading of rapture, equanimous, mindful and clearly aware, he feels bliss.

stages.name: catuttha jhāna
stages.description: Pleasure and pain abandoned: neither-painful-nor-pleasant, purity of mindfulness through equanimity; in-and-out breathing ceases in it.

stages.name: ākāsānañcāyatana
stages.description: Perception of form ceases; reached by removing the kasiṇa and attending to the space left.

stages.name: viññāṇañcāyatana
stages.description: The perception of infinite space ceases.

stages.name: ākiñcaññāyatana
stages.description: The perception of infinite consciousness ceases; the attainment the bodhisatta learned from Āḷāra Kālāma.

stages.name: nevasaññānāsaññāyatana
stages.description: The perception of nothingness ceases; the attainment learned from Uddaka Rāmaputta, which the bodhisatta left because it did not lead to awakening.

stages.name: saññāvedayitanirodha (nirodha-samāpatti)
stages.description: Perception and feeling cease; the non-occurrence of consciousness and its concomitants by progressive cessation, attained only by non-returners and arahants who have the eight attainments.
stages.band_note: B6 because the commentarial tradition restricts it to noble persons who have already seen (non-returners and arahants); it is an abiding, not itself the final liberation.

equivalents.note: Graded absorptions dropping coarser factors; not claimed identical.
The Laṅkāvatāra's four dhyānas grade meditation by its object rather than by factors.

notes: The canonical list is AN 9.32 (Pali root checked locally); each attainment can also be a basis for insight (AN 9.36). The Buddha passed through all nine, up and down, at his final nibbāna (DN 16 6.8-6.9). The Abhidhamma's fivefold jhāna scheme splits the second jhāna (cpt:five-jhanas-abhidhamma).

name: The seven purifications (satta visuddhi)

stages.name: sīla-visuddhi
stages.description: Fourfold purity: Pātimokkha restraint, restraint of the senses, purity of livelihood, proper use of requisites.

stages.name: citta-visuddhi
stages.description: The eight attainments with their access; for the pure-insight practitioner, momentary concentration.
stages.band_note: B4 as access and absorption (the pure-insight vehicle's momentary concentration is B3-B4).

stages.name: diṭṭhi-visuddhi
stages.description: Defining mentality-materiality by characteristic, function, manifestation and proximate cause; no being or person found apart from them, as 'chariot' is a mere term.
stages.band_note: Mundane insight with conditioned objects: B4 under this unit's rule (B5 reserved for the first supramundane seeing).

stages.name: kaṅkhāvitaraṇa-visuddhi
stages.description: Discerning the conditions of mentality-materiality in the three times; one possessed of it has found a footing in the dispensation (a 'lesser stream-enterer').

stages.name: maggāmagga-ñāṇadassana-visuddhi
stages.gloss: purification by knowledge and vision of what is and is not the path
stages.description: Comprehension of formations as impermanent, painful, not-self; at the tender knowledge of rise and fall ten imperfections (illumination, knowledge, rapture …) arise and are recognized as not the path.

stages.name: paṭipadā-ñāṇadassana-visuddhi
stages.gloss: purification by knowledge and vision of the way
stages.description: Insight reaching its culmination in eight knowledges (rise and fall, dissolution, terror, danger, dispassion, desire for deliverance, reflection, equanimity about formations) with conformity as ninth.

stages.name: ñāṇadassana-visuddhi
stages.description: The knowledge of the four supramundane paths; change-of-lineage, which takes nibbāna as object, stands between the sixth and seventh.
stages.band_note: B5 for the first path (stream-entry); the same purification comprises the higher paths (B6) and the path of arahantship ending in B7.

stages.name: anupādā parinibbāna
stages.description: The goal for which the holy life is lived; each purification serves the next like King Pasenadi's relay of seven chariots.

equivalents.note: The insight knowledges are distributed over purifications 3-7.
Pa-Auk's teaching follows the Visuddhimagga order (U37 bands its mundane insight B5-B6; see cpt:path-map-correspondence).
Purification 1 = virtue, 2 = concentration, 3-7 = understanding.

notes: MN 24 names the seven and the chariot simile; the Visuddhimagga builds its entire structure on them. The last stage (anupādā parinibbāna) is the goal MN 24 names and is added to close the map.

name: The sixteen insight knowledges (soḷasa ñāṇa)

stages.name: nāmarūpa-pariccheda-ñāṇa
stages.description: Distinguishing the noted object from the noting mind; mentality and materiality defined, no self apart from them.

stages.name: paccaya-pariggaha-ñāṇa
stages.description: Seeing their conditionality through the three times; doubt overcome.

stages.name: sammasana-ñāṇa
stages.description: Comprehending formations as impermanent, painful, not-self (unpleasant sensations are often prominent — Mahāsi).

stages.name: udayabbaya-ñāṇa
stages.gloss: knowledge of rise and fall (tender, then mature; the ten imperfections arise at its tender stage)
stages.description: Seeing arising and passing; lights, rapture, tranquillity, strong faith may appear and must not be taken for the path.
stages.band_note: Mundane insight: B4 under this unit's rule; U37's pth:pa-auk-path puts mundane insight at B5-B6.

stages.name: bhaṅga-ñāṇa
stages.description: Only the vanishing of formations is seen.

stages.name: bhaya-ñāṇa
stages.description: Formations appear fearful, like a burning house.

stages.name: ādīnava-ñāṇa
stages.description: Formations seen as full of danger.

stages.name: nibbidā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Disenchantment with all formations.

stages.name: muñcitukamyatā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Wish to escape formations, as a man in a burning house seeks the way out.

stages.name: paṭisaṅkhā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Re-observing formations by the three characteristics in order to be freed.

stages.name: saṅkhārupekkhā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Neutral, effortless noting of formations; the three doors of liberation; insight leading to emergence.

stages.name: anuloma-ñāṇa
stages.description: Conforms to the preceding knowledges and to the requisites of awakening.

stages.name: gotrabhū-ñāṇa
stages.description: Passes from the worldling lineage to the noble lineage, taking nibbāna as object.
stages.band_note: Threshold: takes nibbāna as object but is not yet path; banded with the path (B5).

stages.name: magga-ñāṇa
stages.description: The supramundane path abandoning fetters (first path: personality view, doubt, clinging to rules).

stages.name: phala-ñāṇa
stages.description: The fruit immediately following the path.

stages.name: paccavekkhaṇa-ñāṇa
stages.description: Reviewing path, fruit, nibbāna, defilements abandoned and remaining.
stages.band_note: B5 after the first path; for each higher path the series recurs and belongs to B6, ending with arahantship (B7).

equivalents.note: Knowledges 1-2 fall in purifications 3-4, 3-4 in 5, 4-12 in 6, 13-16 around and in 7.
Mahāsi Sayadaw's practical account of the same knowledges through noting.
Sarvāstivāda: heat, peak, patience and supreme mundane quality precede the path of seeing, as mundane insight precedes the path here.

notes: Correction to the unit brief: the count of sixteen is post-canonical — the Visuddhimagga distributes these knowledges over purifications 3-7 and the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha counts ten insight knowledges (comprehension → conformity); the list of sixteen is the later manual count taught in Burma (e.g. by Mahāsi Sayadaw). The Paṭisambhidāmagga's list of seventy-three knowledges is a different scheme.

name: The four stages of awakening and the eight noble persons

stages.name: sotāpattiyaṅga
stages.description: Association with good persons, hearing the true Dhamma, wise attention, practice in accordance with the Dhamma.

stages.name: sotāpatti-magga (saddhānusārī / dhammānusārī)
stages.description: The path moment: the Dhamma-eye arises — 'whatever is subject to arising is subject to cessation'.

stages.name: sotāpanna
stages.description: By the destruction of three fetters (personality view, doubt, clinging to rules and observances): not subject to the lower realms, fixed in destiny, bound for awakening; confirmed confidence in the three jewels and the virtues dear to the noble ones ('the mirror of the Dhamma').

stages.name: sakadāgāmi-magga
stages.description: The second path.

stages.name: sakadāgāmī
stages.description: Three fetters destroyed and lust, hate and delusion weakened: returns to this world once and makes an end of suffering.

stages.name: anāgāmi-magga
stages.description: The third path, abandoning the five lower fetters (with sensual desire and ill will), for instance by seeing the aggregates in a jhāna as impermanent and turning to the deathless.

stages.name: anāgāmī
stages.description: The five lower fetters destroyed: spontaneously reborn (in the Pure Abodes), attaining final nibbāna there without returning from that world.

stages.name: arahatta-magga
stages.description: The fourth path, abandoning the five higher fetters (lust for form and the formless, conceit, restlessness, ignorance).

stages.name: arahant
stages.description: By the destruction of the effluents, having realized for himself here and now the effluent-free freedom of mind and freedom by wisdom: 'birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, done is what was to be done'.

equivalents.note: Sarvāstivāda has the same four fruits and eight persons, with a different account of the path of seeing (fifteen/sixteen moments).
Stream-entry corresponds to the path of seeing, the higher paths to the path of cultivation, arahantship to no-more-learning, in the Abhidharma and Mahāyāna presentations.
Stream-entry and Jain right view are both the first irreversible seeing that bounds the remaining births; the not-self teaching and the Jain soul-doctrine are not reconciled by this.

notes: Stage 1 (factors for stream-entry) is added as the entry named in SN 55.5. The canonical eight persons are AN 8.59 (Pali root checked locally); DN 16 2.7 gives the defining formulas (checked locally). Lay followers attain all three lower fruits in DN 16.

name: The seven factors of awakening arising in sequence (MN 118)

stages.name: sati-sambojjhaṅga
stages.description: When the four establishments of mindfulness are practised, unremitting mindfulness is established — the first factor.

stages.name: dhammavicaya-sambojjhaṅga
stages.description: Arises from the preceding factor when the four establishments of mindfulness are developed; supported by seclusion, dispassion and cessation, ripening in relinquishment.

stages.name: vīriya-sambojjhaṅga
stages.description: Arises from the preceding factor when the four establishments of mindfulness are developed; supported by seclusion, dispassion and cessation, ripening in relinquishment.

stages.name: pīti-sambojjhaṅga
stages.description: Arises from the preceding factor when the four establishments of mindfulness are developed; supported by seclusion, dispassion and cessation, ripening in relinquishment.

stages.name: passaddhi-sambojjhaṅga
stages.description: Arises from the preceding factor when the four establishments of mindfulness are developed; supported by seclusion, dispassion and cessation, ripening in relinquishment.

stages.name: samādhi-sambojjhaṅga
stages.description: Arises from the preceding factor when the four establishments of mindfulness are developed; supported by seclusion, dispassion and cessation, ripening in relinquishment.

stages.name: upekkhā-sambojjhaṅga
stages.description: Arises from the preceding factor when the four establishments of mindfulness are developed; supported by seclusion, dispassion and cessation, ripening in relinquishment.

stages.name: vijjā-vimutti
stages.description: The seven factors, developed and cultivated, fulfil true knowledge and liberation.

equivalents.note: MN 118's sixteen steps fulfil the establishments of mindfulness, which fulfil these factors.
Another canonical sequence leading through rapture, tranquillity and concentration to knowledge and liberation.

notes: A sequence stated by the sutta itself ('each arises from the preceding'); the factors are also developed together.

name: Mahāsi Sayadaw's progress of insight through noting

stages.name: sīla-visuddhi
stages.description: The meditator first purifies conduct (precepts) before the retreat.

stages.name: citta-visuddhi by khaṇika-samādhi
stages.gloss: purification of mind by momentary concentration
stages.description: Continuous, precise noting of whatever arises (beginning with the rising and falling of the abdomen) builds momentary concentration strong enough for insight, in place of jhāna.
stages.ref: Practical Insight Meditation; Progress of Insight
stages.band_note: B3; the tradition holds that momentary concentration does the work of access concentration for the pure-insight practitioner.

stages.name: knowledges 1-3
stages.description: The noted object and the noting mind are distinguished, their conditionality seen, and they are comprehended as impermanent, painful, not-self; unpleasant sensations are often prominent.

stages.name: knowledge 4
stages.description: Bright lights, rapture, tranquillity, happiness, strong faith and quick noting may appear; attachment to them is the corruption of insight to be noted and passed.

stages.name: knowledges 5-10
stages.gloss: dissolution, fearfulness, misery, disgust, desire for deliverance, re-observation
stages.description: Only vanishing is seen; formations appear fearful, full of danger and wearisome; a desire for deliverance arises; re-observation.

stages.name: knowledge 11
stages.description: Noting proceeds by itself, smoothly and without effort, neither delighting nor fearing, and can last long.

stages.name: knowledges 12-13
stages.description: Insight leading to emergence culminates in conformity and then in change-of-lineage.
stages.band_note: Conformity is B4 and change-of-lineage B5 on pth:sixteen-insight-knowledges; grouped here as the threshold.

stages.name: knowledges 14-15
stages.description: The noted objects and the noting mind cease: the cessation of formations (nibbāna) is experienced.

stages.name: knowledge 16 and after
stages.gloss: reviewing; fruition attainment; the higher paths
stages.description: Reviewing knowledge follows; the meditator may practise entering fruition and continue insight for the higher paths.

equivalents.note: Same sixteen knowledges presented through the practice of noting.

notes: Post-1800 teacher (recent). Kept separate from pth:sixteen-insight-knowledges because Mahāsi's account describes the stages as they appear in noting practice (momentary concentration instead of jhāna, typical experiences at each stage). Grouping of knowledges follows the chapter's own grouping as recalled; moderate confidence on the grouping.

name: The five paths (pañca-mārga): accumulation, preparation, seeing, cultivation, no-more-learning

stages.name: saṃbhāra-mārga
stages.description: Entered with the uncontrived mind of awakening (or, for the lesser vehicles, renunciation); accumulation of merit and wisdom by hearing, reflection, ethics and calm abiding.
stages.band_note: B2 as accumulation and training; its entry (bodhicitta) is B0 and its greater level includes calm abiding (B3-B4).

stages.name: prayoga-mārga
stages.description: Four stages — heat, peak, patience, supreme mundane quality — in which, by insight joined to calm, the grasped and then the grasper are seen as empty/mind-only; 'the aids to penetration'.
stages.band_note: B4: insight that still has a conceptual object (this unit's rule); the direct seeing comes at the next path.

stages.name: darśana-mārga
stages.description: The first direct, non-conceptual seeing of reality: the dharmadhātu directly perceived, free of duality; sixteen moments (eight acceptances and eight knowledges) regarding the four truths; the first bodhisattva ground.

stages.name: bhāvanā-mārga
stages.description: The remaining grounds (2-10): non-conceptual knowledge purifying the buddha-qualities and subsequent knowledge maturing beings, until the diamond-like concentration.

stages.name: aśaikṣa-mārga / niṣṭhā-mārga
stages.description: The final transformation of the basis, stainless of all obscurations: buddhahood (for the lesser vehicles, arhatship); the dharma-body.

stages.name: buddha-karma
stages.gloss: the activity of the buddhas (in Gampopa's sequence)
stages.description: The buddhas' activity benefits beings spontaneously and without conceptual thought, like the sun shining or a wish-fulfilling jewel; it is effortless and uninterrupted.
stages.band_note: Not one of the five paths; added from Gampopa's Jewel Ornament (and the Ratnagotravibhāga), which follow the paths with buddhahood and its activity.

equivalents.note: Xuanzang's five stages of the path to cognition-only (資糧, 加行, 通達, 修習, 究竟) are the five paths.
The Sarvāstivāda path has the same preparatory aids (heat, peak, patience, supreme mundane) and the paths of seeing, cultivation and no-more-learning.
Path of seeing = first ground; path of cultivation = grounds 2-10; no-more-learning = buddhahood.
In the Abhidharma and Mahāyāna presentations stream-entry is on the path of seeing and arhatship at no-more-learning.
Padampa Sangye arranges Pacification along these five paths.
Kagyu masters correlate the four yogas with the five paths in differing ways (Moonbeams).

notes: Pan-Mahāyāna frame (Yogācāra sources, Abhisamayālaṃkāra, Tibetan lamrim and grounds-and-paths literature; also applied to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas). Stage 6 is outside the five and marked as such.

name: The ten grounds of the bodhisattva (daśabhūmi) of the Daśabhūmika Sūtra

stages.name: pramuditā
stages.description: Joy at being born into the Tathāgata's family; freed from five fears; ten great vows; giving predominates.
stages.band_note: B5: the first ground is the path of seeing.

stages.name: vimalā
stages.description: The ten wholesome paths of action kept purely even in their subtle forms; morality predominates.

stages.name: prabhākarī
stages.description: Seeing conditioned things as impermanent and burning; the four dhyānas, formless attainments, immeasurables and superknowledges; patience predominates.

stages.name: arciṣmatī
stages.description: The thirty-seven wings of awakening cultivated; views of self burned away; vigour predominates.

stages.name: sudurjayā
stages.description: The four noble truths and two truths understood in all their forms; worldly arts mastered for beings' sake; meditation predominates.

stages.name: abhimukhī
stages.description: Dependent origination examined: 'this triple world is mind only'; the three doors of liberation before him; wisdom predominates.

stages.name: dūraṅgamā
stages.description: Skilful means; entering cessation moment by moment without realizing it; living in the world while beyond it.

stages.name: acalā
stages.description: Acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas; effortless non-conceptual knowledge; roused by the buddhas from resting in peace to remember his vows; vow predominates.
stages.band_note: B6; Candrakīrti and later Tibetan scholastics hold that the afflictive obscurations are exhausted here (an arhat's freedom), while cultivation continues for the knowledge obscurations.

stages.name: sādhumatī
stages.description: Knowing beings' minds and faculties perfectly; teaching with the four analytical knowledges; power predominates.

stages.name: dharmameghā
stages.description: Consecrated by the rays of all buddhas as a great lord of the dharma, he rains the dharma on beings like a cloud; knowledge predominates.
stages.band_note: The band scheme mentions 'dharmamegha as culmination' under B8; the tenth ground's raining of the dharma has the character of activity (B8), but it precedes buddhahood in the sūtra, so it is banded B6, as on U40's pth:madhyamakavatara-ten-grounds.

stages.name: buddha-bhūmi
stages.description: The ground beyond the ten: perfect buddhahood with the three bodies.

equivalents.note: Candrakīrti's Madhyamakāvatāra follows the same ten grounds and perfections; bands identical.
The Lokottaravāda Mahāvastu has a different list of ten grounds (durārohā …).
The Bodhisattvabhūmi's thirteen abodes include the ten grounds within a longer series.
The East Asian fifty-two stages place the ten grounds after the ten faiths, abodes, practices and dedications.
Ground 1 = path of seeing; 2-10 = path of cultivation.

notes: Names as in the Daśabhūmika (Skt.). The Saṃdhinirmocana pairs the ten grounds with ten perfections (six + means, vow, power, knowledge) and adds a buddha-ground; stage 11 is that ground.

name: The nine stages of settling the mind (navākārā cittasthiti) leading to calm abiding

stages.name: cittasthāpana / sems 'jog pa
stages.description: The mind is placed on the object (by the power of hearing). [power; attention: hearing; forced attention]

stages.name: saṃsthāpana / rgyun du 'jog pa
stages.description: Placed for a little longer (power of reflection). [power; attention: reflection; forced attention]

stages.name: avasthāpana / glan te 'jog pa
stages.description: Distraction noticed quickly and the mind patched back (mindfulness). [power; attention: mindfulness; interrupted attention]

stages.name: upasthāpana / nye bar 'jog pa
stages.description: The mind withdrawn inward ever more; the object no longer lost (mindfulness). [power; attention: mindfulness; interrupted attention]

stages.name: damana / dul bar byed pa
stages.description: Delighting the mind in concentration by seeing its qualities (alertness). [power; attention: alertness; interrupted attention]

stages.name: śamana / zhi bar byed pa
stages.description: Quelling displeasure toward concentration (alertness). [power; attention: alertness; interrupted attention]

stages.name: vyupaśamana / rnam par zhi bar byed pa
stages.description: Pacifying even subtle attachment, sinking and agitation as they arise (effort). [power; attention: effort; interrupted attention]

stages.name: ekotīkaraṇa / rtse gcig tu byed pa
stages.description: Continuous concentration with a little effort at the start (effort). [power; attention: effort; uninterrupted attention]

stages.name: samādhāna / mnyam par 'jog pa
stages.description: Effortless, spontaneous concentration (familiarity). [power; attention: complete familiarity; spontaneous attention]
stages.band_note: B3: before pliancy arises the ninth state is only a 'likeness' of calm abiding (LRCM).

stages.name: śamatha proper (with pliancy)
stages.description: After the ninth state mental and then physical pliancy arise with their joy; when the joy settles the mind rests stably on its object at will — calm abiding proper, the preparation for the first dhyāna.

equivalents.note: The Śrāvakabhūmi's seven attentions continue from calm abiding into the dhyānas.
Kamalaśīla's stages embed the same nine settlings.
Mahāmudrā śamatha uses the nine settlings (Moonbeams).
Calm abiding proper corresponds to access to the first dhyāna in both Abhidharma systems.

notes: Sanskrit names as in the Śrāvakabhūmi (sthāpayati, saṃsthāpayati, avasthāpayati, upasthāpayati, damayati, śamayati, vyupaśamayati, ekotīkaroti, samādadhāti; nominal forms given); Tibetan as in the Lamrim literature. The six powers and four attentions are given per stage as the Lamrim Chenmo distributes them.

name: The stages of the path for persons of the three scopes (lam rim; skyes bu gsum)

stages.name: reliance on the spiritual teacher
stages.description: Proper reliance on a qualified teacher in thought and deed.

stages.name: leisure and endowment
stages.description: Its great value and rarity: free of the eight unfree states, with the ten endowments.

stages.name: small scope: death and the lower realms
stages.description: Mindfulness of death (certain, its time uncertain, only dharma helps) and the sufferings of the lower realms.

stages.name: small scope: refuge and karma
stages.gloss: refuge and the ethics of action
stages.description: Going for refuge (from fear of the lower realms and faith); the four characteristics of karma; abandoning the ten non-virtues.
stages.band_note: Refuge itself is B0; the ethics of karma is B1.

stages.name: middle scope: the faults of saṃsāra and renunciation
stages.description: The eight and six sufferings, the origin in the afflictions; renunciation arises when one wishes for liberation day and night like a prisoner.
stages.band_note: B0: each scope opens with a turning of the mind; the Lamrim is therefore non-monotonic by design.

stages.name: middle scope: the three trainings
stages.description: Ethics, concentration and wisdom, with ethics as their foundation.

stages.name: great scope: the mind of awakening
stages.description: The seven-point cause-and-effect instruction and the exchange of self and other; adopting the aspiring and engaging mind of awakening by ritual.

stages.name: great scope: the deeds
stages.gloss: six perfections and four ways of gathering
stages.description: The bodhisattva vow; the six perfections ripen one's own continuum, the four ways of gathering ripen others.

stages.name: calm abiding
stages.description: The nine mental states, six powers and four attentions, to calm abiding proper with pliancy.

stages.name: insight
stages.description: Identifying the object of negation and establishing the selflessness of persons and phenomena by Prāsaṅgika reasoning; insight proper when analysis itself induces pliancy and calm and insight are unified.
stages.band_note: B4 by this unit's rule: the union of calm and insight on emptiness is still conceptual (it marks the path of preparation in Tsongkhapa's account); the direct seeing is the path of seeing (B5, pth:five-paths).

stages.name: entering the Vajrayāna
stages.description: Having trained in the paths common to sūtra and tantra, one should enter the Vajrayāna: empowerment from a qualified master, guarding vows and pledges, the two stages.
stages.band_note: Unbanded: the Lamrim hands over to the Ngagrim; see pth:vajrayana-two-stages.

equivalents.note: Tsongkhapa's condensation: renunciation (middle scope), the mind of awakening (great scope), the correct view (insight).
Gampopa's Jewel Ornament (Kagyu) follows the same Kadam stages.
The Sakya 'parting from the four attachments' condenses the same scopes.
The Nyingma outer preliminaries cover the same ground as the small and middle scopes.
Expands stage 7.

notes: Atiśa's Bodhipathapradīpa defines the three persons (v2-5); Tsongkhapa's Lamrim Chenmo gives the full stages. The first two stages are 'the foundation'; each scope begins with its own turning of mind, which is why the bands return to B0 three times.

name: The four yogas of Mahāmudrā with their twelve levels (phyag chen rnal 'byor bzhi)

stages.name: rtse gcig (ekāgra) — lesser
stages.description: Resting in clarity and emptiness with stability; experiences of bliss, clarity and non-thought; the nature not yet seen without veil.
stages.band_note: B4: stable calm with the nature glimpsed but not yet seen without veil; some correlate one-pointedness with the paths of accumulation and preparation.

stages.name: rtse gcig (ekāgra) — middling
stages.description: Middling level of one-pointedness.

stages.name: rtse gcig (ekāgra) — greater
stages.description: Greater level of one-pointedness.

stages.name: spros bral (niṣprapañca) — lesser
stages.description: The mind's nature seen as free of arising, abiding and ceasing, beyond extremes; appearances not yet fully one with mind.
stages.band_note: Many Kagyu masters place the path of seeing at simplicity (some at its lesser, some at its greater level); Moonbeams records the differing views.

stages.name: spros bral (niṣprapañca) — middling
stages.description: Middling level of simplicity / freedom from elaboration.

stages.name: spros bral (niṣprapañca) — greater
stages.description: Greater level of simplicity / freedom from elaboration.

stages.name: ro gcig (ekarasa) — lesser
stages.description: Appearances and mind, saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, are of one taste in the nature; subtle clinging to the meditation remains.

stages.name: ro gcig (ekarasa) — middling
stages.description: Middling level of one taste.

stages.name: ro gcig (ekarasa) — greater
stages.description: Greater level of one taste.

stages.name: sgom med (abhāvanā) — lesser
stages.description: Nothing to meditate and no meditator; the natural state without contrivance; at its greatest, the dharmakāya fully manifest.

stages.name: sgom med (abhāvanā) — middling
stages.description: Middling level of non-meditation.

stages.name: sgom med (abhāvanā) — greater
stages.description: Greater level of non-meditation.
stages.band_note: Greater non-meditation = buddhahood (the fruition dharmakāya).

equivalents.note: Expands stage 7 of U46's Moonbeams map.
Tilopa's torrent–river–ocean describes the same deepening in three images.
Kagyu masters correlate the four yogas with the five paths and ten grounds differently; Moonbeams records the views.
Drikung's fivefold Mahāmudrā arranges the same practice by five points rather than stages.

tradition_objection: Mahāmudrā teachers stress that the nature of mind is not produced by the yogas: 'no path to travel', 'if you attain non-attainment you attain Mahāmudrā' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā); the four yogas describe the ripening of recognition and are said to arise in different orders for gradual and simultaneous persons.
notes: The twelve levels are given as in Dakpo Tashi Namgyal's Moonbeams; descriptions of the middling and greater levels are kept generic because they were not recalled with confidence. The correlations with the five paths differ among Kagyu masters (tea:moonbeams-of-mahamudra:pt.2/7).

name: The four visions of Direct Crossing (thod rgal gyi snang ba bzhi)

stages.name: chos nyid mngon sum
stages.description: Presupposing recognition of awareness (rig pa) through the master's introduction and stability in cutting through, the display of the ground begins to appear directly as light.
stages.band_note: B5 as the first direct manifestation; the recognition of awareness on which it rests (cutting through) is itself B5 on pth:yeshe-lama-path.

stages.name: nyams gong 'phel
stages.description: The visionary display increases and develops.

stages.name: rig pa tshad phebs
stages.description: Awareness reaches its full extent; the display is complete.

stages.name: chos nyid zad pa
stages.description: All appearances dissolve into dharmatā; the texts speak of the body of light (rainbow body) as its sign.

equivalents.note: The four visions are the direct-crossing stage of Jigme Lingpa's Yeshe Lama map (U45).
Both describe the ripening of the recognition of mind's nature to its exhaustion/non-meditation; neither tradition treats them as identical systems.
Both are completion-level practices in which appearances of light arise and are recognized as the mind's own display; methods and views differ.

tradition_objection: Dzogchen holds that awareness is primordially complete and is not produced by stages: the Kunjed Gyalpo says there is nothing to be done, no view to meditate and no path to traverse, and 'whatever is meditated is my sickness'; the four visions are the self-display of spontaneous presence, not a ladder of attainment. Direct crossing is taught only to those stable in cutting through.
notes: RESTRICTED: direct crossing (thod rgal) is a restricted practice; only the names of the four visions and the texts' own framing are recorded — no postures, gazes, lamps or other method details. Stage names are the standard ones (moderate-to-high confidence); precise textual loci in the Seventeen Tantras are not given (chapter-level refs only).

name: The six-branch yoga (ṣaḍaṅga-yoga) of the Kālacakra

stages.name: pratyāhāra (sor sdud)
stages.description: The senses withdrawn; practised in darkness and against the open sky, ten signs appear in order — smoke, mirage, fireflies, lamp, blaze, moon, sun, darkness, lightning (kalā), drop — the 'empty forms'.

stages.name: dhyāna (bsam gtan)
stages.description: Stabilizing on the empty forms that have appeared, without imagining them ('meditation on an imagined image is not meditation for yogins').

stages.name: prāṇāyāma (srog rtsol)
stages.description: The winds of the left and right channels are brought into the central channel.
stages.band_note: Restricted practice: summary only.

stages.name: dhāraṇā ('dzin pa)
stages.description: The winds, having entered, are held in the central channel at the centres.
stages.band_note: Restricted practice: summary only.

stages.name: anusmṛti (rjes dran)
stages.description: The blazing of inner heat and the arising of bliss joined with the empty form (the 'form of the deity').
stages.band_note: B4 (still with the support of empty form); some presentations place it at the end of the path of preparation.

stages.name: samādhi (ting nge 'dzin)
stages.description: Immutable bliss inseparable from empty form; the 21,600 moments of immutable bliss consume the 21,600 karmic winds.
stages.band_note: Spans B5-B7: its first moments are counted as the path of seeing, its completion as buddhahood (low confidence on the exact correlation with the grounds).

stages.name: fruit: the Ādibuddha's gnosis
stages.description: Immutable great bliss complete; the body of empty form; the gnosis of the Ādibuddha, 'without beginning or end', not a creator.

equivalents.note: Same six branch-names in the same order (Guhyasamāja 18.138); Kālacakra gives them its own content.
Six limbs with five shared names (tarka in the Maitrī where the Kālacakra has anusmṛti).
The six branches are the Kālacakra's completion stage.

tradition_objection: The Kālacakra tradition (esp. Jonang) teaches the six branches only after the Kālacakra empowerment, the preliminaries and the lineage instructions; its wind practices are not to be attempted otherwise (Tāranātha).
notes: RESTRICTED: completion-stage energy practice — summary and the tradition's own warnings only; no methods, postures, durations or retention details. Tāranātha takes the branches in pairs: the first pair makes the empty forms appear, the middle pair brings the winds into the central channel, the last pair produces bliss and immutable bliss.

name: Pacification (zhi byed) arranged along the five paths

stages.name: tshogs lam
stages.description: Pacification instructions for the path of accumulation (preliminaries, main practice and conclusion); details not recalled.

stages.name: sbyor lam
stages.description: Instructions for the path of joining; details not recalled.

stages.name: mthong lam
stages.description: Instructions for the path of seeing; details not recalled.

stages.name: sgom lam
stages.description: Instructions for the path of meditation; details not recalled.

stages.name: mi slob lam
stages.description: The fruit; details not recalled.

equivalents.note: The general five-path frame applied to Pacification.

notes: Defined because U48's teachings and practices reference this id. Only the frame (five paths, each with preliminaries, main practice and conclusion) is recalled; the contents of each path's instructions are not, and are left as gaps.

name: Kuoan's ten oxherding pictures (Shiniu tu)

stages.name: xun niu 尋牛
stages.description: The herdsman searches through the wild grasses; the preface: the ox has never been lost — by turning his back on awakening he became estranged.

stages.name: jian ji 見跡
stages.description: Through the sūtras and teachings he sees the footprints: the many vessels are all gold, but he has not yet entered the gate.
stages.band_note: B2: understanding through sūtras and teachings, 'not yet entered the gate'.

stages.name: jian niu 見牛
stages.description: Hearing a sound he glimpses the ox itself: it is not elsewhere, it was always there.
stages.band_note: B5: the first glimpse of one's own nature (kenshō).

stages.name: de niu 得牛
stages.description: He seizes it, but it is wild and old habits pull it back; he must use the whip.
stages.band_note: B6: after seeing, old habits still pull the ox back to the grasses.

stages.name: mu niu 牧牛
stages.description: With rope and whip at hand the ox becomes gentle; thoughts arise one after another, but awakening makes them true.

stages.name: qi niu gui jia 騎牛歸家
stages.description: The struggle over, he rides home playing the flute.

stages.name: wang niu cun ren 忘牛存人
stages.description: At home the ox is forgotten; whip and rope lie idle; he sits alone at ease.
stages.band_note: B6: the object gone, the subject still remains.

stages.name: ren niu ju wang 人牛俱忘
stages.description: Whip, rope, person and ox are all empty — an empty circle.
stages.band_note: B7: the empty circle — ordinary and holy both vanish.

stages.name: fan ben huan yuan 返本還源
stages.description: Returning to the source: the rivers flow and the flowers are red of themselves.
stages.band_note: B7: seeing things as they are (the rivers flow, the flowers are red) without striving.

stages.name: ru chan chui shou 入鄽垂手
stages.gloss: entering the marketplace with helping hands
stages.description: Bare-chested and barefoot he enters the marketplace with wine gourd and staff; the withered trees burst into bloom.
stages.band_note: B8: return to the world to benefit others.

sources.ref: pictures 1-10 with verses and Ciyuan's prefaces

equivalents.note: Puming's series ends in the empty circle (Kuoan's 8); Kuoan adds returning to the source and entering the marketplace.
Another Chan map ending in return to the world of distinctions.
