Seeing the ox then taming it matches 'sudden awakening, gradual cultivation'.

tradition_objection: The first preface says the ox was never lost: the pictures describe the ending of an estrangement, not the gaining of something new; Chan teachers use them as skilful means (P6), not as a fixed ladder.
notes: Kuoan Shiyuan (廓庵師遠, 12th c., Linji/Yangqi line), with prefaces by Ciyuan; Xuzangjing X1269 (Kuoan's series) is the text used by U42's teachings. Distinguish from Puming's whitening-ox series (pth:puming-ten-oxherding-pictures).

name: Jinul's sudden awakening and gradual cultivation (tono chŏmsu)

stages.name: seeking buddha in one's own mind
stages.description: The three realms burn like a house on fire; to escape transmigration nothing is better than seeking buddha, and buddha is the mind — not outside, not apart from this body.

stages.name: tono 頓悟 (haeo 解悟)
stages.description: When a good friend points the way and in one thought one turns back the light and sees one's original nature — empty, calm, numinous knowing — it lacks nothing.
stages.band_note: B5; Jinul (after Zongmi) calls this an understanding-awakening, distinct from the realization-awakening at the end.

stages.name: chŏmsu 漸修
stages.description: Habit-energies cannot be removed at once, so relying on awakening one cultivates gradually, like an infant growing up: noticing thoughts as they arise ('do not fear thoughts arising, only fear being slow to notice'); the dual cultivation of samādhi and prajñā as substance and function of the self-nature; for the penetrated, effortless 'just thus'.

stages.name: chŭng 證 (chŭngo 證悟)
stages.description: 'All sages first awaken, then cultivate, and through cultivation realize'; phenomena are exhausted step by step as the frozen pond melts; powers appear only through gradual cultivation and are not to be used.

equivalents.note: Jinul adopts Zongmi's 'sudden awakening followed by gradual cultivation' and cites his frozen-pond simile.
Seeing the ox then taming it.
Immediate recognition for some, graded means for others.

tradition_objection: Jinul says the gates are in essence only two, sudden awakening and gradual cultivation; even 'sudden awakening, sudden cultivation' of the highest faculties rests on cultivation in past lives; principle is awakened to all at once and only phenomena are removed step by step — so the awakening itself is not a rung of a gradual ladder.
notes: Rests entirely on the Susim kyŏl (T48n2020, verified in CBETA by U42). Jinul's shortcut approach of investigating the hwadu (kyŏngjŏl mun, from the Kanhwa kyŏrŭi ron) is not included: that text is not available locally.

name: Dōgen's unity of practice and realization and the way-ring of continuous practice (shushō ittō; gyōji dōkan)

stages.name: hosshin 発心
stages.description: The first of the four phases of the way-ring; for Dōgen it is not before the others but circles with them without gap.
stages.band_note: B0 by what it names; Dōgen denies that it precedes the others (way-ring).

stages.name: shugyō 修行 — shikan taza
stages.description: Practice is practice-in-realization (shō-jō no shu): the beginner's wholehearted practice of the way is the whole of original realization; just sit, thinking not-thinking.
stages.band_note: B6 in Dōgen's own terms ('practice on top of realization'), not as a preparatory stage (B2-B4); it is listed before awakening because Dōgen lists it so.

stages.name: bodai 菩提
stages.description: 'That the myriad things come forward and verify the self is awakening'; awakening is like the moon in water — the moon does not get wet, the water is not broken.
stages.band_note: Banded B5 by what it names; for Dōgen it is not after practice.

stages.name: nehan 涅槃
stages.description: The fourth phase of the ring, returning without gap to arousing the mind; 'when the myriad dharmas are without self there is no delusion, no awakening, no buddhas, no beings'.

equivalents.note: Both are Zen maps, but Dōgen rejects treating practice as a means to a later awakening, which the pictures' sequence suggests.
Jinul puts cultivation after awakening; Dōgen makes them one — 'practice on top of realization' is close to Jinul's order, but Dōgen denies any sequence.
Both traditions deny that practice produces what is already complete ('the Way is fundamentally complete'; the all-creating king has nothing to do).

tradition_objection: Dōgen denies that this is a ladder: 'to think practice and realization are not one is a non-Buddhist view'; the four phases form a ring without the slightest gap, and the Way 'is fundamentally complete — why depend on practice and realization?', yet 'if there is the slightest gap, heaven and earth are far apart'. The bands therefore do not describe an order of attainment; they only record which band each named phase would occupy on other maps.
notes: The four phases are from the Gyōji fascicle (text not available locally; moderate confidence on wording). Bands are deliberately non-monotonic (B0, B6, B5, B7) to show that Dōgen places 'practice' where other maps place post-awakening cultivation.

name: Zhiyi's six identities (liuji 六即)

stages.name: liji 理即
stages.description: One moment of mind is the principle of the tathāgatagarbha — empty, provisional and middle — present in all beings unknowing.
stages.band_note: Starting condition (the ground in all beings), unbanded; Zhiyi's point is that it is already 'identical' with bodhi.

stages.name: mingziji 名字即
stages.description: Hearing from a good friend or the sūtras of the one real bodhi and understanding in words that all dharmas are buddha-dharma; faith in the dharma-nature.

stages.name: guanxingji 觀行即
stages.description: Mind and speech in accord; contemplation unceasing, though not yet in accord with principle (later Tiantai: the five grades of disciples).

stages.name: xiangsiji 相似即
stages.description: The more one contemplates the clearer, like an archer nearing the target; purification of the six senses; ignorance subdued; wisdom resembling the middle way (later: the ten faiths).
stages.band_note: B4: resembling, not yet true, wisdom — the analogue of the path of preparation.

stages.name: fenzhenji 分真即
stages.description: Ignorance first broken, buddha-nature seen, the treasury opened (the abode of arousing the mind), and so on through forty-one stages to equal awakening; manifesting bodies to save beings.
stages.band_note: B5 at its first moment; its further stages up to equal awakening are B6 (with B8 activity: manifesting bodies for beings).

stages.name: jiujingji 究竟即
stages.description: Equal awakening turns into wondrous awakening; wisdom's light complete; the great nirvāṇa, nothing more to cut.

equivalents.note: Zhiyi maps the perfect teaching's stages onto the six identities: resemblance = ten faiths; partial truth = the forty-one stages from the first abode to equal awakening; ultimate = wondrous awakening.
Resemblance ~ preparation; partial truth begins with the first seeing of buddha-nature.

tradition_objection: Zhiyi's point is identity (ji 即): every stage, even the ordinary person's, is identical with bodhi in principle, and the stages exist only to prevent both discouragement and arrogance ('beginning with the ordinary removes doubt; ending with the sage removes arrogance'); he says the six identities are used only for the perfect teaching.
notes: All six names and their explanations verified in the local CBETA text of the Mohe zhiguan (T1911, 10b12-10c24); the text reads 分真即 (partial truth), not the later 分證即. Zhiyi also correlates the Dazhidulun's five bodhis with these stages (10c25ff.).

name: The fifty-two stages of the bodhisattva path (ten faiths + forty-two stages of worthies and sages)

stages.name: shixin 十信
stages.description: Preliminary to the forty-two: practised for one to ten kalpas before entering the abodes; they can still regress.
stages.band_note: B0 as faith; later Tiantai puts them at the 'resemblance' identity (B4).

stages.name: shizhu 十住
stages.gloss: the ten abodes (nature of habituation, xizhongxing)
stages.description: From the abode of arousing the mind to the abode of consecration; the first of the 'three worthy' groups.
stages.band_note: B2 in the sūtra's own scheme (worthies, not yet sages); in Zhiyi's perfect teaching the first abode is already the first seeing of buddha-nature (B5).

stages.name: shixing 十行
stages.description: From the practice of joy onward.

stages.name: shi huixiang 十迴向
stages.gloss: the ten dedications (nature of the path, daozhongxing)
stages.description: Dedicating merit; the last group of worthies before the sagely grounds.
stages.band_note: B4: the threshold group before the grounds (the analogue of preparation).

stages.name: shidi 十地
stages.description: The ten bodhisattva grounds; entry into the sages.
stages.band_note: B5 at the first ground, B6 for grounds 2-10.

stages.name: dengjue 等覺
stages.description: The forty-first stage, equal to buddhahood but for a last trace.

stages.name: miaojue 妙覺
stages.description: The forty-second ground, the mind of quiescence, clear like space; buddhahood.

equivalents.note: Stage 5 is the ten grounds.
The Śūraṅgama's fifty-five stages add the dry-wisdom ground and the four aids to the same sequence.
Zhiyi places these stages within the six identities.

notes: Group names and the six natures verified in CBETA T1485 (1012b25-26; 1014b29-c01; 1015c09). The sūtra counts forty-two stages of worthies and sages with the ten faiths as preliminary; 'fifty-two' is the common East Asian count including the faiths. Tiantai (perfect teaching) and Huayan place the first seeing earlier (at the first abode) than this sūtra's own scheme; the bands follow the sūtra's division into worthies (abodes, practices, dedications) and sages (grounds).

name: Zongmi's ten phases of awakening (悟十重) in the Chan Preface

stages.name: dunwu 頓悟 (jiewu 解悟)
stages.description: Meeting a good friend, one understands the original enlightened true mind; the four elements are not self, the aggregates empty; faith in one's own suchness and the Three Jewels.
stages.band_note: B5 as the understanding-awakening; the phases after it are all 'cultivation after awakening' (B6).

stages.name: fa beizhi yuan 發悲智願
stages.description: Pledging to realize bodhi.
stages.band_note: B0 in kind (arousing the mind) but placed by Zongmi after awakening, within cultivation (B6).

stages.name: suifen xiuxi 隨分修習
stages.description: Giving, precepts, patience, vigour and calming-and-contemplation; the root of faith grows.
stages.band_note: B1-B3 in kind; after awakening (B6).

stages.name: da putixin xianfa 大菩提心顯發
stages.gloss: the great mind of awakening manifests
stages.description: The great bodhicitta becomes manifest.

stages.name: zhi faxing 知法性
stages.description: Knowing the dharma-nature to be free of stinginess and the rest.
stages.band_note: Phases 5 and 6 are not clearly separated in the digital rendering of the chart.

stages.name: suishun xiu liudu, wofa shuangwang 隨順修六度 我法雙亡
stages.gloss: the perfections in accord; self and dharmas both forgotten
stages.description: Practising the six perfections in accord with the dharma-nature; by samādhi and prajñā self and dharmas are forgotten — always empty, always illusory.

stages.name: yu se zizai 於色自在
stages.description: All interfused.

stages.name: yu xin zizai 於心自在
stages.description: Illuminating everything.

stages.name: jiujing jue 究竟覺
stages.description: Means fulfilled, one thought in accord; the first arising of mind awakened, free of subtle thought.

stages.name: da jue zun 大覺尊
stages.description: No separate initial awakening; one with the pure mind-source, responding in countless ways and abiding in the dharma-realm; seeing all beings as equally awakened.
stages.band_note: B7, with the B8 aspect of responsive activity (應用塵沙).

equivalents.note: Jinul condenses Zongmi's sequence into sudden awakening, gradual cultivation and realization.

notes: Zongmi pairs ten phases of delusion (from the original enlightened mind, through non-awakening, to the reception of karmic results) with ten phases of awakening that overturn them in reverse order. The phase names used here are descriptive labels drawn from the chart's text as read in CBETA (T2015); they are not a fixed list of titles, and the division of phases 5-6 is uncertain.

name: Kūkai's ten abodes of mind (jūjūshin)

stages.name: ishō teiyō shin 異生羝羊心
stages.gloss: the mind of the ordinary person like a ram
stages.description: Driven by appetite for food and sex like a goat.
stages.band_note: Starting condition, unbanded.

stages.name: gudō jisai shin 愚童持齋心
stages.gloss: the mind of the foolish child keeping fasts
stages.description: The first stirring of ethics (worldly moral teaching).

stages.name: yōdō mui shin 嬰童無畏心
stages.gloss: the fearless mind of the infant
stages.description: Religion aimed at birth in heaven (the non-Buddhist and heavenly vehicles).

stages.name: yuiun muga shin 唯蘊無我心
stages.gloss: the mind that knows only aggregates, no self
stages.description: The śrāvaka vehicle.
stages.band_note: Doxographical rank of a vehicle; unbanded (cf. pth:nyingma-nine-vehicles).

stages.name: batsugō inshu shin 拔業因種心
stages.gloss: the mind that uproots the seed of karma
stages.description: The pratyekabuddha vehicle.
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: taen daijō shin 他縁大乘心
stages.gloss: the Mahāyāna mind concerned with others
stages.description: Hossō (Yogācāra).
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: kakushin fushō shin 覺心不生心
stages.gloss: the mind awakened to the unborn
stages.description: Sanron (Madhyamaka).
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: ichidō mui shin 一道無爲心
stages.gloss: the mind of the one way without action
stages.description: Tendai.
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: gokumu jishō shin 極無自性心
stages.gloss: the mind of the ultimate absence of own-nature
stages.description: Kegon.
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: himitsu shōgon shin 秘密莊嚴心
stages.description: Shingon: the mind as the maṇḍala; becoming a buddha in this very body.
stages.band_note: B7 as the text's goal (sokushin jōbutsu).

equivalents.note: Both rank the Buddhist vehicles in an ascending doxography culminating in the author's own tantric vehicle.

tradition_objection: Kūkai reads the ten both 'vertically' (as ascending stages, the first nine exoteric and the tenth esoteric) and 'horizontally' (all nine as aspects contained within the tenth, the maṇḍala); the ladder is a classification of teachings by depth (P5), not a practitioner's required sequence.
notes: From memory: the ten names are well known, but the text is not available locally (Taishō vol. 77). Banded only where the abode describes a practitioner's ethical or religious condition (2, 3) or the goal (10); the abodes that rank Buddhist schools are left unbanded, following U45's pth:nyingma-nine-vehicles.
